subject: Biology
description: Respiratory system, breathing mechanism, gaseous exchange, alveoli

questions.stem: GASEOUS EXCHANGE in lungs takes place at:
questions.explanation: ALVEOLI = ~300 MILLION tiny air sacs in lungs (~75 m² total surface area, like a tennis court!). VERY THIN walls (1 cell thick); SURROUNDED by capillaries (also 1 cell thick) — facilitates gas exchange. O₂ diffuses from alveoli → blood; CO₂ diffuses from blood → alveoli (down concentration gradient). Pathway: nose → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. PNEUMONIA = alveoli filled with fluid. EMPHYSEMA = alveoli walls broken (smoking damage). COVID-19 ARDS = alveoli inflammation.

options.option_text: Stays still / does not move at all
Relaxes and rises upward in chest
Spasms and twitches in irregular motion

questions.explanation: INHALATION: DIAPHRAGM (dome-shaped muscle below lungs) CONTRACTS → flattens → moves DOWN. Intercostal muscles also contract → ribs UP + OUT. Result: thoracic cavity expands → pressure decreases → air FLOWS IN. EXHALATION (passive at rest): diaphragm RELAXES → moves UP; ribs come DOWN; cavity contracts → pressure increases → air OUT. Active exhalation (during exercise) uses abdominal muscles. HICCUP = involuntary diaphragm spasm.

questions.stem: OXYGEN is mainly transported in blood by:

options.option_text: Platelets in tiny droplets in blood

questions.explanation: HAEMOGLOBIN — protein in RBCs; binds O₂ (each Hb has 4 heme groups, each with iron — Fe; binds 4 O₂ molecules). ~98% of O₂ transported via Hb (only ~2% dissolved in plasma). HbO₂ = oxyhaemoglobin (bright red); deoxyhaemoglobin (dark red, blueish). CO₂ TRANSPORT: ~70% as bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻) in plasma, ~20% bound to Hb (carbamino), ~10% dissolved. CARBON MONOXIDE binds Hb 200× more strongly than O₂ → blocks O₂ transport → CO POISONING (vehicle exhaust, faulty heaters, fires).

questions.stem: TIDAL VOLUME (normal breathing volume) of an adult is about:
questions.explanation: TIDAL VOLUME (TV) = ~500 mL per breath at rest. RESPIRATORY RATE (RR) = ~12-20 breaths/min. Minute ventilation = TV × RR ≈ 6 L/min. INSPIRATORY RESERVE VOLUME (IRV) ≈ 3000 mL — extra air can inhale forcibly above tidal. EXPIRATORY RESERVE VOLUME (ERV) ≈ 1100 mL. RESIDUAL VOLUME (RV) ≈ 1200 mL — air ALWAYS in lungs (cannot exhale fully). VITAL CAPACITY = TV + IRV + ERV ≈ 4600 mL (max breath in + out). TOTAL LUNG CAPACITY ≈ 5800 mL = VC + RV. Spirometer measures these.

questions.stem: Disease causing inflammation of bronchi (often from smoking, asthma, infection) is:
questions.explanation: BRONCHITIS — inflammation of bronchi (lining); ACUTE (~weeks, usually viral); CHRONIC (months/years; defined as productive cough most days for 3+ months in 2 consecutive years; mostly from smoking — part of COPD). Symptoms: cough, mucus, wheezing, shortness of breath. EMPHYSEMA — alveolar wall destruction (also COPD; smoking). PNEUMONIA — alveoli infection (bacterial, viral, fungal); COVID-19 was a viral pneumonia. TUBERCULOSIS (TB) — bacterial (M. tuberculosis); India has world's highest TB burden (~28% of global cases). Vaccine: BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin).

78% N₂, 21% O₂, plus traces of others
50% O₂ and 50% N₂ in our air
78% O₂ and 21% N₂ in our air

questions.explanation: ATMOSPHERIC AIR composition: N₂ 78.08%, O₂ 20.95%, Ar 0.93%, CO₂ 0.04% (rising), trace gases. EXHALED AIR: O₂ ~16% (used some), CO₂ ~4% (added some), N₂ unchanged, water vapour higher, slightly warmer. Note: only O₂ is used for cellular respiration, but body inhales whole atmosphere. PURE O₂ inhalation for prolonged time is TOXIC (oxygen toxicity, esp. above 50%) — damages alveoli (ROS — reactive oxygen species). Used short-term in medical emergencies.

questions.stem: Cellular respiration occurs primarily in which organelle?
questions.explanation: MITOCHONDRIA = 'POWERHOUSE OF THE CELL'. Site of CELLULAR RESPIRATION: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + ATP (energy). Two membranes; inner folded into CRISTAE → larger surface for ATP synthesis. Stages: GLYCOLYSIS (cytoplasm; glucose → pyruvate; 2 ATP); KREBS / TCA cycle (mitochondrial matrix; CO₂ released); ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN (inner membrane; major ATP production via O₂). Total ~30-32 ATP per glucose. Mitochondria have OWN DNA (mtDNA) — endosymbiont theory (originally bacteria engulfed by ancestor cell). Inherited only from MOTHER (sperm mtDNA destroyed at fertilization).
